attempts.note: The previous attempt named no dataset (reason given: I could not identify with certainty any public dataset of per-capitulum sunflower parastichy crossing angles or floret-coordinate data that has a verifiable landing page or DOI. The large portals I know (GBIF, NCBI, Dryad, Zenodo) hold sunflower genomes, occurrence records and phenotyping data, but I could not confirm a specific record that gives floret positions or spiral crossing angles. Naming one from memory would risk a fabricated identifier. The test needs a new image set or a floret-coordinate deposit.).

The previous attempt named no dataset (reason given: I could not identify, and so could not verify, any public dataset of sunflower floret coordinates or parastichy crossing angles with a resolvable landing page or DOI. The portals I know well (GBIF, NCBI, Dryad, Zenodo, figshare) hold sunflower genomes, occurrence records and agronomic phenotyping data. None is a confirmed record of per-floret positions or spiral crossing angles. Naming one from memory would risk a fabricated identifier. The test needs a new capitulum image set with floret segmentation, or a floret-coordinate deposit from a phyllotaxis study.).

The previous attempt named no dataset (reason given: I could not confirm any specific public dataset of 3D red-cell surface reconstructions, with matched hypotonic and isotonic conditions, that has a landing page and DOI I am sure resolves. Candidates I recall include holotomography and quantitative phase imaging data, the Chula RBC-12 image set and Broad Bioimage Benchmark Collection images. I could not verify their URLs or DOIs, and 2D smear images cannot give mean curvature. Naming an unverified identifier would risk a fabricated citation, so I report null. The test could be run if a verified deposit of 3D RBC tomograms (Zenodo or figshare) is later identified.).

The previous attempt named no dataset (reason given: I could not find and verify a public deposit of 3D red-cell shape reconstructions (holotomography or similar) that includes both isotonic and hypotonic conditions and has a landing page and DOI I can confirm. One search turned up only journal articles on red-cell holotomography and an unrelated organoid dataset. Two-dimensional smear images cannot give mean curvature. I am reporting null rather than naming an unverified identifier. The test could be run if a verified deposit of 3D RBC tomograms with osmotic conditions is identified.).
